notes:
Summary of account: Bridgepoint is an EU-headquartered KM/analytics provider building a cross-lingual RAG layer for enterprise customers (legal, pharma, telco verticals). Key priorities: per-language recall and precision tuning, <200ms p95 embedding similarity latency for EU queries, reranker p95 <400ms, total cost per query target <$0.03 for 3MLU request pattern. They care deeply about language coverage (FR, ES, DE, JA, NL, PT) and expect per-language relevance benchmarks.

What we learned in calls:
- They currently run a polyglot index of ~12M docs (pdfs, KB, support transcripts) and plan to ingest up to 200M by end of year across clients.
- Their prototype uses dense vectors stored in a managed ANN but struggles with cross-lingual recall: English queries map well, but Japanese and Portuguese queries see lower recall vs English baseline.
- They want explicit reranking stage: embedding retrieval -> lightweight bilingual reranker -> final ranker tuned per language.
- Routing needs: EU-first routing for GDPR customers, fallback to US-hosted models for reduced-cost tiers.
- Cost sensitivity: finance wants per-query cost breakdown for embeddings, ANN ops, and reranker compute; target is to get below €0.025 per 1k-token RAG call on average.

CRM style notes / call snippets: 
- "If we can't show per-lang lift we'll not move forward" — Head of Search (call 2026-01-25).
- "Need an apples-to-apples for JA recall before procurement" — ML lead.
- "Prefer a Dedicated plan for compliance + predictability" — CTO.

Technical constraints and wishlist:
- Per-language tokenization and normalization pipelines (ja-mecab, de-compound) integrated before embedding stage.
- Ability to pin reranker versions per customer and keep eval artifacts.
- Fine-grained tracing (token-level cost + latency) for production SLA compliance.

Decision signals:
- High: strong product/technical buy-in; POC metrics will drive procurement.
- Low: preference for open models if performance matches, else willing to pay for Redwood-verified models.
